name: Andrej Karpathy
contribution: Made neural-network internals and language-model training easier to study and reproduce through small, readable implementations, from scalar autograd to raw C/CUDA training.

name: Georgi Gerganov
contribution: Created the llama.cpp and whisper.cpp projects, bringing language-model and speech inference to ordinary local hardware through portable C/C++ implementations. The projects now live under ggml-org.

name: Mario Zechner
contribution: Created Pi, a minimal, extensible coding-agent harness with an embeddable SDK, making the agent loop available for custom workflows and applications. The project now lives under earendil-works.

name: Simon Willison
contribution: Built LLM, a CLI and Python library that makes local and hosted models scriptable through a shared interface and plugins, supporting repeatable experiments and everyday developer workflows.

name: Yohei Nakajima
contribution: Explored autonomous task planning with the original BabyAGI in 2023, then self-building agents with its successor. These compact experiments make agent-loop ideas available to inspect and adapt; they are not production frameworks.

name: Anomaly
contribution: Builds OpenCode and models.dev, pairing an open coding agent with shared model capability and pricing data that other tools can reuse.

name: Anthropic
contribution: Builds Claude Code, bringing codebase exploration, edits, command execution and Git workflows into a conversational coding-agent interface.

name: ggml
contribution: Develops llama.cpp and whisper.cpp with portable inference, quantization and hardware backends, making local language and speech models practical across CPUs and GPUs.

name: Hugging Face
contribution: Provides reusable model implementations through Transformers and parameter-efficient adaptation through PEFT, reducing the work needed to run and fine-tune pretrained models.

name: LangChain
contribution: Builds LangGraph for long-running, stateful agent orchestration and Deep Agents for planning, filesystem access and delegation, making those execution patterns reusable.

name: Model Context Protocol
contribution: Maintains shared protocol infrastructure and reference servers for connecting models to tools and data, so integrations can be reused across compatible clients rather than rebuilt for each harness.

name: OpenAI
contribution: Builds Codex CLI, an open coding-agent implementation that developers can run locally and inspect, extending model assistance into repository edits and command execution.

name: Vercel
contribution: Builds the provider-agnostic AI SDK and the filesystem-first Eve framework, giving TypeScript developers reusable interfaces for model calls, agent tools and durable agent applications.
